fields.rationale: States cluster by how tightly they bind to the CDR exam: those that name it exclusively, those that accept CDR or leave a board-approval escape hatch, those that define their own exam with no CDR reference, those with in-house state-run exams, and those requiring multiple distinct exams.

States cluster by the primary mechanism they use: most require equivalent standards from the other state, some add a clean disciplinary record as a distinct element, some explicitly accept CDR registration as a standalone pathway, a few delegate details entirely to the board, one uses a formal reciprocity agreement, one grants only temporary/limited practice rights, and Florida relies on an endorsement/background-check pathway.

The commission may not adopt a new rule relating to the scope of practice of or a health-related standard of care for dietitians unless the rule has been proposed by the advisory board; the commission retains authority for final adoption.
